versions.short: The bill would raise the debt limits that apply to two kinds of bankruptcy filers. For small businesses, the cap on total debts that can qualify for the small business bankruptcy process would rise to $7,500,000, excluding debts owed to affiliates or insiders, with at least half of the debt tied to the business's own commercial activities; businesses that are part of a larger affiliated group above that amount, or that file reports with the Securities and Exchange Commission, or that are affiliates of such companies, would not qualify. For individuals, the limit for filing under chapter 13, the repayment-plan form of bankruptcy, would rise to debts totaling less than $2,750,000, applying to an individual or an individual and spouse with regular income, excluding stockbrokers and commodity brokers. The changes would apply to any case started on or after the date the bill is enacted.
